// 01 — ABOUT

Thinking like the architect and the attacker

I thrive on analyzing complex digital threats and engineering practical solutions to stop them. I enjoy building secure systems that combine software engineering with cybersecurity principles — because building great software is meaningless if it isn't secure.

Cybersecurity fascinates me because it lets me hold two perspectives at once: the architect designing the system, and the attacker probing it for weaknesses. I enjoy understanding vulnerabilities before malicious actors can exploit them.

My long-term vision is to engineer secure-by-default systems capable of defending critical digital infrastructure against evolving cyber threats — eventually growing into the role of Lead Security Engineer.

CAREER OBJECTIVE

To start my career in Cyber Security and apply technical knowledge to protect digital systems — eager to learn, grow, and contribute to a secure IT environment.

// 04 — FEATURED PROJECT

PortScan

A high-performance web-based port scanner capable of scanning all 65,535 ports in under three seconds — built to explain risk, not just report numbers.

portscan — session
$ portscan --target 10.0.0.4 --ports all --mode rustscan
▸ scanning 65,535 ports...
▸ 22/tcp open — ssh (OpenSSH 8.9)
▸ 443/tcp open — https
▸ 3306/tcp filtered — mysql
▸ scan complete in 2.81s
  • RustScan integration with a FastAPI backend and SQLite scan history
  • Real-time, live TCP & UDP scanning with progress feedback
  • Port and service detection across open, closed, and filtered states
  • Beginner-friendly security explanations for every finding
  • Responsive interface built for quick, repeatable audits

WHY THIS MATTERS

Instead of surfacing raw numbers, PortScan explains why a port is open, what service commonly runs there, the realistic risk it introduces, and the mitigation worth applying — turning a scan result into something a non-expert can act on.
